source.title: Steering Sparse Autoencoder Latents to Control Dynamic Head Pruning in Vision Transformers (Student Abstract)

record.tranche_reason: It replaces the model's residual embedding with an SAE reconstruction and measures task accuracy and pruning behavior, bearing on whether omitting the SAE error loses meaningful model behavior. It does not use the original study's error-predictability measurements.
record.gate_note: The reported SAE-steering outcomes are not included: they measure intentionally induced pruning changes, not whether the SAE error carries behavior. The reconstruction comparison is included. The study does not compare reconstruction error with size-matched random errors or measure error predictability across SAE sizes.
record.test_reason: As a control, the study replaces the final-layer CLS embedding with its SAE reconstruction, dropping the error term, before the pruning decision network. It reports the resulting change in accuracy and head usage. Its steering analysis also drops the error, so this result bears on V5 in a new setting: a ViT dynamic-pruning gate. It is a narrow sanity check, not a dedicated dark-matter test.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also use this result as a control: they conclude the steering effects come from latent steering rather than reconstruction artifacts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a k-sparse autoencoder on a ViT residual embedding and tests reconstruction replacement in dynamic head pruning; it does not reproduce the original study's dark-matter error analyses.
record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Student Abstract)
record.problems: Evidence on reconstruction is reported for one ViT-Small setting and the text provides no uncertainty estimates or random-error comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Steering-strategy results and class-specific steering examples in Experiments and the Appendix are omitted because they report intentionally induced pruning behavior, not whether SAE error carries behavior when it is omitted.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation is not measured.
Error norms are not measured across SAE sizes; only one SAE size (8x, k=64) is used.
There is no comparison with size-matched random errors, and no effect on the model's loss is measured.
The error is not decomposed into linear and nonlinear parts.
Circuit analyses are not tested, and error is not substituted into the model's main computation. Only the input to the pruning gate is replaced, in one layer and one model.
No alternative architectures or training objectives are compared.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the reader's 'challenges' label to 'limits_scope' because the error is removed only from a small decision-network input in one layer, one model and one SAE. The steering results are correctly excluded because they intentionally induce pruning changes.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error norms across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than size-matched random errors.
The distinction between linearly predictable and nonlinear SAE error, and their relation to dictionary learning.
The study measures accuracy and dynamic head usage for one SAE reconstruction setting, but does not test circuit analyses or compare steering with and without retaining an explicit error term.
Whether dark matter is an artifact of SAE training choices or shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

relationships.condition: ViT-Small fine-tuned on CIFAR-100. A top-k SAE (8x, k=64) reconstruction of the final-layer CLS token is fed only to the head-pruning decision network.
relationships.reason: Dropping the SAE error changed accuracy by −0.12% and head usage by +0.025 (r1, r2). The error carried negligible function for this narrow pruning-gate readout. This is a single setting with no uncertainty reported, so it qualifies V5's generality rather than broadly refuting it.
relationships.display_finding: Removing the error changed accuracy by −0.12% and head usage by +0.025, indicating negligible functional loss for the pruning decision network.
